They weigh exactly the same — a kilogram is a kilogram, regardless of the material. A kilogram of feathers and a kilogram of steel both have a mass of one kilogram, so on a scale they'd balance perfectly.

This is a classic trick question that plays on our intuitions. It feels like steel should be "heavier" because it's denser — a kilogram of steel would fit in your hands as a small, compact block, while a kilogram of feathers would be an enormous, fluffy pile.
